summary: A responsive warm editorial recipe scaling calculator lets visitors edit an initial four-serving recipe, calculate scaled quantities, validate serving counts, switch list views, reset the example, and read a short explanation.

journeys.title: A visitor scales the initial four-serving recipe to six servings

steps.expect: the initial four-serving recipe and serving controls are visible
the scaled ingredient list visibly shows the correct six-serving quantities

acceptance: With original servings at 4 and desired servings at 6, the visible scaled list shows rice — 450 g, water — 900 ml, and salt — 3 tsp.

journeys.title: A visitor adds and removes a decimal-quantity ingredient

steps.expect: the ingredient editor is visible

steps.action: enter a decimal ingredient name and quantity
steps.expect: the new ingredient name and decimal quantity are displayed in their fields
the ingredient unit field displays tsp
cumin is added to the active recipe list with its decimal quantity
the added decimal ingredient is visibly recalculated for six servings
the cumin row is removed while the three initial scaled ingredient rows remain visible

acceptance: A decimal ingredient quantity of 1.5 tsp can be added and visibly scales to cumin — 2.25 tsp when the recipe changes from 4 to 6 servings.
Removing cumin leaves the three initial ingredient rows visible.

journeys.title: A visitor switches between original and scaled ingredient lists

steps.expect: the recipe list view switcher is visible
a six-serving scaled recipe is visible
the original ingredient quantities are visible
the scaled ingredient quantities are visible

acceptance: After scaling from 4 to 6 servings, the Original view visibly shows rice — 300 g and the Scaled view visibly shows rice — 450 g.

journeys.title: A visitor receives clear feedback for invalid serving counts

steps.expect: both serving count inputs are visible

visibleText: Scaled quantities are unavailable until both serving counts are greater than zero.
steps.expect: an inline blank-count message is shown and calculated quantities are unavailable

visibleText: Servings must be greater than zero.
Scaled quantities are unavailable until both serving counts are greater than zero.
steps.expect: an inline zero-count message is shown and no stale calculated result is displayed

steps.action: enter a negative desired serving count
visibleText: Servings must be greater than zero.
Scaled quantities are unavailable until both serving counts are greater than zero.
steps.expect: an inline negative-count message is shown and no stale calculated result is displayed

visibleText: Servings must be greater than zero.
Scaled quantities are unavailable until both serving counts are greater than zero.
steps.expect: the original servings control shows clear inline invalid-count feedback

acceptance: Blank, zero, and negative serving counts visibly show inline feedback and replace calculated quantities with the unavailable-results message.

journeys.title: A visitor restores the initial four-serving example

steps.expect: the reset control and initial recipe are visible
the calculator shows a changed scaled recipe
the visible ingredient rows and serving controls are restored to the initial four-serving example

acceptance: Reset visibly restores original servings and desired servings to 4 and restores rice — 300 g, water — 600 ml, and salt — 2 tsp.

journeys.title: A visitor reads how the recipe scaling calculation works

steps.action: open the how it works page
steps.expect: a short explanation of the scaling formula is visible
the calculator is visible again

acceptance: The How it works page is reachable from the calculator and visibly provides a route back to the calculator.

routes.name: Calculator
routes.purpose: Enter serving counts, edit recipe ingredients, view original or scaled quantities, and reset the initial example.

routes.name: How it works
routes.purpose: Explain the scaling formula and provide navigation back to the calculator.

entities.name: calculatorState
relationships: ingredients is the ordered original recipe list and scaledIngredients is its transient calculated counterpart

rules: The calculator and How it works page are available without signing in.

operations.description: Revalidate serving counts and regenerate transient scaled quantities whenever either serving count changes.

responsibilities.behavior: When originalServings and desiredServings are both present and greater than zero, calculate scalingFactor as desiredServings divided by originalServings, calculate every scaled ingredient quantity as its original quantity multiplied by scalingFactor, set isScalingValid true, set scaledResultsAvailable true, and clear servingsFeedback. When either count is blank, zero, or negative, set isScalingValid false, set scaledResultsAvailable false, clear the visible calculated quantities, and set servingsFeedback to the applicable inline message.

operations.description: Append a transient ingredient row from the ingredient entry controls and update calculated quantities when servings are valid.

responsibilities.behavior: When ingredientName, ingredientQuantity, and ingredientUnit are supplied, append the entered row to ingredients, clear ingredientFeedback, and regenerate scaledIngredients using the current scaling factor when servings are valid. When any required ingredient entry value is absent, do not change ingredients and set ingredientFeedback to a visible inline message.

operations.description: Remove the ingredient row selected by its visible remove control from the transient recipe.

responsibilities.behavior: Remove the ingredient row selected by the clicked remove control and regenerate scaledIngredients from the remaining ingredients when servings are valid.

operations.description: Restore all calculator values to the initial four-serving recipe example.

responsibilities.behavior: Replace the current serving values, ingredient rows, calculated rows, list view, and feedback with the initial four-serving rice, water, and salt example.

integrations.name: none
integrations.purpose: The calculator uses local transient browser state only and makes no external API, payment, storage, or backend requests.

states.loading: The initial recipe example is immediately visible without remote loading.
states.empty: When every ingredient has been removed, the ingredient area visibly shows 'No ingredients yet. Add one above.'
states.validation: A blank original or desired serving count visibly shows 'Enter a serving count.'; a zero or negative count visibly shows 'Servings must be greater than zero.'; while invalid, calculated quantities are replaced by 'Scaled quantities are unavailable until both serving counts are greater than zero.'
states.error: Attempting to add an ingredient without its name, quantity, or unit visibly shows 'Complete the ingredient name, quantity, and unit.' and does not add a row.
states.success: Valid serving count changes visibly update the scaled ingredient quantities.

states.loading: Calculator controls and navigation are visible immediately.
states.success: At phone-width and desktop-width viewports, controls remain visible and usable without horizontal page scrolling.

acceptance.statement: With original servings set to 4 and desired servings set to 6, the visible scaled list contains rice — 450 g, water — 900 ml, and salt — 3 tsp.
Blank, zero, and negative serving counts visibly show inline feedback and the visible unavailable-results message instead of stale calculated quantities.
A decimal ingredient quantity of 1.5 tsp added to the recipe visibly scales to cumin — 2.25 tsp after desired servings changes from 4 to 6.
The Original and Scaled controls visibly switch between rice — 300 g and rice — 450 g after scaling from 4 to 6 servings.
Reset visibly restores the three initial ingredient rows and both serving controls to 4.
The calculator and How it works pages remain usable without horizontal scrolling at phone-width and desktop-width browser viewports.

deferred.item: Saved recipes, reload recovery, and recipe history
deferred.reason: The request specifies a calculator and does not request persistence.
The request explicitly requires no login.

deferred.item: Payments and external recipe, nutrition, or shopping APIs
deferred.reason: The request explicitly excludes payments and external APIs.
